events.summary:
The team has done strong work establishing the shape of the incident: a single sharp step at ~10:58-11:02Z, exchange-gateway degrading BEFORE order-service (10:58 bucket vs order-service's first error at 11:02:45Z), all 349 order-service errors being one signature (504 on the exchange-gateway placeOrder call), no internal saturation on order-service, and a rollback that changed nothing (flat ~31% errors and ~5.3s p99 through 12:58Z). That correctly kills the reporter's suspicion (H1, dep-5333) and the cfg-2290 red herring (H3). The direction of causation is well supported: order-service is a victim, the fault is at or below exchange-gateway.

However, the ranking itself does not hold up. H4 (network/mesh/infrastructure) is ranked FIRST at 0.30 while H2 (exchange-gateway's upstream dependency failure) is ranked at 0.00 — yet every verified finding (F11, F14, F17) points directly at H2 and nothing verified supports H4. F14 is the single earliest signal: exchange-gateway's own upstream_error_rate 0.30%→40.87% and upstream_latency_ms 120ms→9400ms, which is upstream-dependent degradation, not mesh-level breakage. H4's supporting set (F7,F9,F15,F16) is all order-service-side symptom and timing data that is equally consistent with H2, and H4 explicitly rests on an unverified assumption ("an infra/mesh change occurred that is not captured by get_deployments/get_config_changes") — the very gap listed as a gap, i.e., absence of evidence being used as evidence. F1/F3 (the only two changes in the window) do not contradict H2 any more than H4, and F1/F3 do not affirmatively support an unobserved mesh event. So the #1 ranking is inverted relative to the evidence, and H2's 0.00 confidence (which should also prevent it from propagating as a top candidate) is wrong.

Remaining blocking evidence is small and obtainable with the 36 tool calls left: (1) the identity/health of exchange-gateway's upstream (was it the external exchange-api partner, and did the external partner fail — e.g. logs/metrics, dependency metadata); (2) exchange-gateway WARN+ logs to distinguish an upstream timeout (slow partner = H2) from connection-refused/DNS/mesh errors (H4); (3) a blast-radius check showing whether other exchange-gateway callers share the exact 10:58Z onset, which would let us rule in exchange-gateway as origin rather than order-service-specific coincidence. The task budget is 36 calls, so this is a cheap and decisive round rather than an unnecessary one.

Note also that the exact deploy timestamp of v2.15.2 was never retrieved (a listed gap), but this does not matter for the ranking because the rollback-with-no-recovery result (F13) already excludes the deploy as causal; I am not requesting more work on that.

Recommend: before accepting anything, (a) re-rank H2 above H4 or justify H4 on evidence, and (b) obtain the three items above. Confidence cap on H4 as currently stated is 0.25.

Grounding: every hop of H2's chain rests on a VERIFIED finding: external-only downstream (F19,F23), zero exchange-gateway changes (F21), earliest signal is exchange-gateway's own upstream_* metrics at 10:58–11:00Z (F14), reachable-but-slow partner proven by 5000ms-connect-timeout signatures AND partner-generated 503s carrying x-partner-request-id=b62798d4 etc. (F24,F25,F29), no connectivity signature (F26), ONWARD circuit-breaker WARN on exchange-api (F27), order-service signature exclusively the placeOrder 504 (F8). critiques.summary:
The team has done strong work establishing the shape of the incident: a single sharp step at ~10:58-11:02Z, exchange-gateway degrading BEFORE order-service (10:58 bucket vs order-service's first error at 11:02:45Z), all 349 order-service errors being one signature (504 on the exchange-gateway placeOrder call), no internal saturation on order-service, and a rollback that changed nothing (flat ~31% errors and ~5.3s p99 through 12:58Z). That correctly kills the reporter's suspicion (H1, dep-5333) and the cfg-2290 red herring (H3). The direction of causation is well supported: order-service is a victim, the fault is at or below exchange-gateway.

However, the ranking itself does not hold up. H4 (network/mesh/infrastructure) is ranked FIRST at 0.30 while H2 (exchange-gateway's upstream dependency failure) is ranked at 0.00 — yet every verified finding (F11, F14, F17) points directly at H2 and nothing verified supports H4. F14 is the single earliest signal: exchange-gateway's own upstream_error_rate 0.30%→40.87% and upstream_latency_ms 120ms→9400ms, which is upstream-dependent degradation, not mesh-level breakage. H4's supporting set (F7,F9,F15,F16) is all order-service-side symptom and timing data that is equally consistent with H2, and H4 explicitly rests on an unverified assumption ("an infra/mesh change occurred that is not captured by get_deployments/get_config_changes") — the very gap listed as a gap, i.e., absence of evidence being used as evidence. F1/F3 (the only two changes in the window) do not contradict H2 any more than H4, and F1/F3 do not affirmatively support an unobserved mesh event. So the #1 ranking is inverted relative to the evidence, and H2's 0.00 confidence (which should also prevent it from propagating as a top candidate) is wrong.

Remaining blocking evidence is small and obtainable with the 36 tool calls left: (1) the identity/health of exchange-gateway's upstream (was it the external exchange-api partner, and did the external partner fail — e.g. logs/metrics, dependency metadata); (2) exchange-gateway WARN+ logs to distinguish an upstream timeout (slow partner = H2) from connection-refused/DNS/mesh errors (H4); (3) a blast-radius check showing whether other exchange-gateway callers share the exact 10:58Z onset, which would let us rule in exchange-gateway as origin rather than order-service-specific coincidence. The task budget is 36 calls, so this is a cheap and decisive round rather than an unnecessary one.

Note also that the exact deploy timestamp of v2.15.2 was never retrieved (a listed gap), but this does not matter for the ranking because the rollback-with-no-recovery result (F13) already excludes the deploy as causal; I am not requesting more work on that.

Recommend: before accepting anything, (a) re-rank H2 above H4 or justify H4 on evidence, and (b) obtain the three items above. Confidence cap on H4 as currently stated is 0.25.

critiques.summary:
All three blockers I raised in round 1 were resolved with verified, decisive evidence, and the ranking has been corrected (H2 0.78 active; H4/H1/H3 rejected, each contradicted by named findings).

Grounding: every hop of H2's chain rests on a VERIFIED finding: external-only downstream (F19,F23), zero exchange-gateway changes (F21), earliest signal is exchange-gateway's own upstream_* metrics at 10:58–11:00Z (F14), reachable-but-slow partner proven by 5000ms-connect-timeout signatures AND partner-generated 503s carrying x-partner-request-id=b62798d4 etc. (F24,F25,F29), no connectivity signature (F26), ONWARD circuit-breaker WARN on exchange-api (F27), order-service signature exclusively the placeOrder 504 (F8). The only non-verified items (partner-side root mechanism; HIST-103 as precedent) are explicitly labeled assumptions/lead and neither carries the conclusion.

Temporal order: onset is tightly established and the cause precedes it — exchange-gateway 10:58Z bucket (p99 131→3017ms), errors 11:00Z, order-service first error 11:02:45Z, and exchange-gateway normal at the 10:48Z deploy minute (F10,F14,F15). Rollback at 11:16Z changed nothing through 12:58Z (F13).

Scope: it explains every affected service without a shared-cause stretch — order-service, api-gateway and market-data-service all step at 11:02Z (F31,F33,F35), i.e. after exchange-gateway's 11:00Z onset, while pricing-engine and the shared components show no step (F30,F32). The implicated change (dep-5333) and the cfg-2290 red herring are both affirmatively excluded (F13, F30), and the competing infra/mesh hypothesis is contradicted rather than merely unproven (F26 + partner 503s prove packets reach a responding partner app; F21 shows no change on our side).

Alternatives: H4's pivotal assumption (unobserved mesh change) is contradicted by the reachability proof; H3 is flat-out falsified by F30; H1 by F8/F13/F15/F16. The residual H2-vs-H4 gap is now a sub-variant question (partner overload vs partner-side network), not a question about the failing hop — the hop is exchange-gateway→exchange-api, which is where the fix (secondary route / vendor escalation) applies.

Data quality: the early exchange-gateway log budget_exhausted gap was retried and filled (T5/F24–F29), and the persistence gap is closed by F28 (same signature at 12:58:32Z). Remaining gaps are non-blocking for the same reason.

Calibration: 0.78 is defensible; I would not go higher only because partner-side causation can never be directly observed (has_telemetry:false), by construction, not for lack of evidence.

challenges.issue: Partner-side root MECHANISM (vendor overload vs vendor-side network) is unobservable because exchange-api has has_telemetry:false (F20); the hypothesis is correctly limited to 'the exchange-api hop is the failing one'. This is an inherent observability limit, not a hole in the chain — the failing hop and the responsible party are established by the partner's own x-partner-request-id 503s (F25).
HIST-103 (F6,F22) is a symptom match and remains a lead, not evidence; it should not be cited as independent support. Its load-bearing value is only that the external-partner identity matches.

The 'slow-but-reachable partner' reading rests on exchange-gateway's view of the partner only; there is no partner-side telemetry to confirm the 503s are the partner's app rather than a middlebox on the egress path synthesizing them. The x-partner-request-id values strongly disfavor this but do not formally exclude it — hence the cap below 0.85.

H4 is not exhaustively excluded by string search alone ('refused'/'dns' = 0 matches does not cover TLS handshake failure, 'no route to host', envoy 'upstream connect error'). However, H4 is independently refuted by the partner returning HTTP 503s with its own request ids (F24,F25), which requires the request to reach a responding partner application.

Exact deploy timestamp of v2.15.2 was never retrieved; this is immaterial because the rollback-no-recovery result (F13, flat ~31% errors and ~5.3s p99 through 12:58Z) independently excludes the deploy as causal. No further work needed on this.
